newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian interest rates seen easing, says ICICI SEC.
newsitem.headline: Indian interest rates seen easing, says ICICI SEC.

text.p: Indian interest rates are headed south in the near term, ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said in a report on Wednesday.
I-Sec said its projections for 1997/98 (April-March) show the banking system is expected to remain in a surplus funds position for most of the first half of the year.
Deposit growth is expected to be in line with Reserve Bank of India's estimate of 800 billion rupees, the report said.

"Further it has been assumed that the incremental credit/deposit ratio for the first half will be around 25 percent (currently 19.80 percent for the first three fortnights of the year), leaving an amount of 260 billion rupees for investment in securities," I-Sec said.

Out of the total of 600 billion rupees of central and state government borrowings, 60 percent is likely to be completed in the first half and (scheduled commercial) banks will subscribe to half of these issues, the report said.
"Hence demand from the banking sectorfor PSU and corporate debt will remain high in the April-September period."

"However, in the second half of 1997/98, as credit to industrial sector accelerates, the amount of investible surpluses available with banks will be lower and some hardening in interest rates can be expected over this period."
Leading Indian banks cut their prime rates by 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points to 14.0-14.5 percent following the central banks first half credit policy statement on April 16.
